Task.title: Task
Task.description: Represents a task or business opportunity within the system.

title.description: Title of the task or business opportunity.

client.description: Name of the client associated with the task.

value.description: Estimated value of the task or business opportunity.

probability.description: Probability of success for the task (percentage).

status.description: Current status of the task (e.g., backlog, prospecting, negotiation, closing, done).

priority.description: Priority level of the task (e.g., low, medium, high).

delegateTo.description: Name of the person to whom the task is delegated.

definition.description: Stores task data. No authorization fields are denormalized, since all data is public in the current version.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to manage tasks and activities. It utilizes a simple collection-based approach for storing task data.  Authorization is based on user ID, although in this design all the data is public, so it is not enforced.  The structure prioritizes simplicity and scalability for a single-user task management system.

**Authorization Independence**:  Currently, authorization independence is not enforced, as the data model does not yet include user-specific ownership.  Future versions would store tasks under `/users/{userId}/tasks/{taskId}` to guarantee private data, and rules will use `request.auth.uid == userId` to give complete ownership of each users' tasks. If this were collaborative, the members map strategy would be used, with membership denormalized to all subcollections to avoid using the expensive `get()` function.

**QAPs**: The structure supports listing all tasks, or limiting tasks by owner (if implemented).
